Emphasized The first week here has been really good so far. It still feels a bit like waiting for the other shoe to drop because classes start on Monday, and that s when the real work begins. But it s been nice having a dorm with just three people instead of 30. It s also nice having access to a tablet and my AirPods in the evenings. The mornings are still early, but I m getting much better sleep and no longer waking up in the middle of the night. I m also about 95% back to normal health. They have vending machines that we re allowed to use during personal time in the barracks, and we re also permitted to use the beverage vending machines at the schoolhouse. I ll have to be careful not to go broke or gain too much weight. A Celsius in the morning is a must to keep from falling asleep. They take dozing off in class very seriously you can get written up for it. Two write-ups result in an Article 15 (military law). The platoon size dynamic is a bit different here. In BCT, there were four platoons of about 55 people each. We did most things together, so that meant 220 people moving at once, which made everything slower. Our platoon here is larger 74 people but the platoons are much more independent. They function like their own mini companies, so things like getting through chow happen a lot faster. One thing I didn t see coming (but maybe should have) is that Human Resources is heavily female-dominated. There are 74 people in the platoon, but only 17 are male. Not sure if that will affect the dynamic at all. I had the fastest two-mile time in our platoon, which was nice. A not-so-nice part is that the fastest runner has to carry the guidon (the small flag at the end of a wooden pole). It s not terrible, but it does mean I m at the front of all formations and have to carry the pole with me everywhere. In Week 5, we should be transitioning to Gold Phase, which will allow us to move around post. That means we ll be able to go to stores, barbershops, Panda Express, and I think there s a movie theater. The last two weeks are considered Gold+ Phase, during which we re allowed to go off-post for the day. Classes start on Monday. We had a brief orientation at the schoolhouse today. It s structured a lot like college, but we can t take any notes out of the classroom to prevent cheating. They also start our GPA at 100 instead of 0.
